value.strategy: Good stock picking, active asset allocation (in and out of equities) at the right time, and a focus on dividend income will add value. Although we advocate low portfolio turnover, there will be times to be active. The Fund’s asset allocation and stock selection reflects uncertainty. The holding in bonds and preference shares will benefit from slower growth and disinflation, the cash and short-dated gilts give us the flexibility to exploit market squalls and protect capital while our equity holdings are biased to consumer goods stocks and utilities that should perform respectably in either a deflationary or inflationary scenario.
value.philosophy: The aim of the Fund is to protect investors’ capital and to increase the value of the Fund year on year. As long term investors, directionless markets are less of a problem for us. We are happy to be patient. It took a patient investor (merely living off dividend income) to await any capital return. Index tracking fund management may be less appealing. Investors are mistaken in believing activity generates returns. This approach of sell low, buy high is no path to riches and, while it may still be the industry standard, it is not a path we intend to follow. The Trojan Fund is an absolute return fund.
value.selection_process: Good stock picking, active asset allocation (in and out of equities) at the right time, and a focus on dividend income will add value. The Fund’s asset allocation and stock selection reflects uncertainty. Equity holdings are biased to consumer goods stocks and utilities. An example holding, Reynolds American, was added based on its merger, upwardly revised cost savings, commitment to a 75% payout ratio, and a prospective dividend yield of over 9%.
value.asset_types: The Trust’s policy is to invest substantially in UK and overseas equities and fixed interest securities. The fund focuses on dividend income. Holdings include bonds and preference shares, cash and short-dated gilts. Equity holdings are biased to consumer goods stocks and utilities. Specific examples include Treasury 5% 2008, War Loan, Treasury 7.5% 2006, BT, NatWest 9% Pref, HBOS 9.25% Pref, Shell T&T, British American Tobacco, Reynolds American, National Grid Transco. Asset allocation includes UK Equities (large cap, mid & small cap), Cash & short-dated Gilts, UK Gilts (long-dated), UK Preference Shares, US Equities.
value.real_objectives: The aim of the Fund is to protect investors’ capital and to increase the value of the Fund year on year. The Fund targets total returns and not income. The investment objective of the Fund is to achieve growth in capital and income in real terms over the longer term. The Trojan Fund is an absolute return fund.
value.fund_history: The Trojan Fund was launched on 30 May 2001. This document is Quarterly No.10, indicating its ongoing operation since launch.
